title: llm-routing-and-caching-prd-scratchpad
content:
Rough PRD / parking-lot: routing + caching features for lower latency and cost (user-facing product angles)

Context / problem statement:
- Many apps see bursty request patterns across tenants and routes. Cold KV cache and suboptimal routing cause tail latency spikes and higher token costs.
- Current Redwood platform has prefix/KV caching primitives in runtime but limited product-level controls for prefetching, routing heuristics, and cross-route cache sharing.
- Need a developer-facing feature set to: reduce p50/p95, lower per-token cost via cache hit-rate, and provide safe fallbacks (model variants, degraded quality) when capacity constrained.

Goals (customer-facing):
- Provide simple toggle/config to enable smarter routing + cache prefetching per-route.
- Improve median latency by 15-30% for <500ms targets on typical chat workloads.
- Increase KV cache hit-rate by 2x for eligible prompt patterns.
- Give clear metrics in Console: cache hit-rate, cost delta, latency distribution, fallback events.

Non-goals:
- Not building a full LLM cache marketplace. No cross-tenant shared caches.
- Not optimizing model weights or training. Focus is on serving-time routing & caching.

Feature rough list (brainstorm):
1) Route-aware prefetching (client-provided hints + automatic inference)
   - If route has recent similar prefix/signature, prefetch KV to warm GPU backend.
   - Heuristics: prefix fingerprinting, similarity by token n-grams, user-specified "prefetch_hint" in request metadata.
   - Controls: per-route prefetch budget (ms token budget), time-to-live for prefetched KV.

2) Priority routing with cost/latency tiers
   - Routes can opt into latency-priority, cost-priority, or balanced modes.
   - Smart router chooses model variant (quantized or full-fp), region, or Dedicated pool fallback.
   - Expose SLOs: target p95 latency, fallback threshold.

3) Adaptive KV cache sharing within customer scope
   - Allow per-customer cache namespace that shares prefixes across routes (opt-in).
   - TTL and privacy controls. Avoid cross-customer sharing.

4) Developer-facing simulation/estimator in Console
   - Given workload sample, the estimator predicts hit-rate, cost savings, and expected latency improvements.
   - Quick A/B to simulate enabling prefetch on a route.

5) Observability and alerting hooks
   - New metrics: prefetch attempts, prefetch success, cache eviction rate, fallback events, model-variant switches.
   - Hook to rollouts: canary prefetch enabled for 1% traffic.

User stories (draft):
- As a product engineer, I want to enable "prefetch-hints" on my chat route so that common conversation prefixes are cached and latency improves for interactive users.
- As an SRE for an enterprise customer, I want to set route-level priorities so critical API calls prefer lower latency model variants and have predictable p95.
- As a Platform engineer, I want to see cache-level observability (hit/miss/eviction) per customer so I can tune budgets and debug regressions.
- As a developer, I want a conservative fallback (model variant) when prefetch budget exhausted, with clear telemetry so I can iterate on prompts.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Feature can be toggled per-route via API + Console (UI stub acceptable for MVP).
- Console displays cache hit-rate and latency delta for routes with prefetch enabled.
- Backend implements a safe prefetch path that does not increase p95 by more than 10% during warmup.
- A/B experiment: enabling prefetch on sample route yields >= 1.5x cache hit-rate and p50 reduction >= 15% on test workload.

Metrics to track:
- p50, p95, p99 latency per route (with and without prefetch)
- KV cache hit-rate (global/per-customer/per-route)
- Tokens served and cost delta estimated (USD/day)
- Prefetch attempts vs successes, prefetch latency overhead
- Fallback count and reason (capacity/model-variant/timeout)

Rollout plan (sketch):
- Phase 0 (internal): white-box tests with runtime team + simulated workloads (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (canary): expose API toggle, enable for internal apps + 3 pilot customers, collect metrics (4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (gradual): UI in Console, estimator tool, expand to more customers, add auto-policy recommendations (6-8 weeks)

Open questions / risks / TODOs:
- Cost model: how to charge for prefetching (prefetch tokens vs reserved budget)? Business + finance input needed.
- Privacy: how to guarantee prefix similarity algorithm doesn't leak PII across routes even within same customer? Need SRE/security review.
- Eviction policy: LRU vs workload-aware; interplay with multi-host KV caches.
- Interaction with batching: prefetch + batching could cause unexpected head-of-line delays. Validate with runtime bench.
- API ergonomics: metadata field name (prefetch_hint vs prefetch.signature). Keep minimal for MVP.

Design notes / quick sketches:
- Prefetch hint: simple base64 sha256 of prefix tokens OR free-form tag. If free-form, allow developer to provide deterministic tag.
- Budget: per-route setting like {prefetch_tokens_per_minute: 1000, max_prefetch_concurrency: 2}.
- Fallback policy: when prefetch miss or budget exhausted -> fall back to model-variant (smaller quantized model) OR route-level degrade to cached response if appropriate.

Links / references:
- Related tickets: JIRA-PRD-789 (placeholder)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/234 (prefetch kernel hooks)
- Earlier scratchpads: users/llm-prefetch-prd-scratchpad-aisha-khan.json

Notes to self (choppy):
- Talk to Aisha re: prefetch kernel interface (runtime).
- Zoe to prototype estimator UI in Console (mockups).
- Ask finance: billing model for prefetch.
- Make small PoC with chat-history-heavy demo app (internal).

Potential quick wins / experiments:
- Server-side only: allow customer to opt into per-customer cache namespace and measure hit-rate improvement without exposing new API fields. Fastest path.
- Estimator MVP: offline script that takes sampled logs and returns hit-rate/cost delta; integrate into Console later.

Longer-term ideas (parking lot):
- Cross-customer anonymized prefix index (probably no).
- Prefetch TTL hints learned via ML (hot-prefix predictor).
- Marketplace of model-variants for fallback with fine-grained cost controls.

-- end --
summary: Personal scratchpad PRD outline for routing + caching features; user stories, acceptance criteria, metrics, rollout sketch, open questions
